Notice.Description: Ofgem's statutory role is to protect the interests of current and future energy consumers and to promote consistently high standards of service across the retail energy market. These insights are essential in helping Ofgem develop effective policies, communications and services. Notice.Title: 2026-026 Cost Allocation and Recovery Review Deliberative Research
Notice.Description: Ofgem is seeking to commission a deliberative research project to explore how consumers think about, assess and respond to different approaches to cost allocation and cost recovery across the energy system. The supplier will conduct market research to examine consumers lived experiences and priorities in relation to affordability, quality of service, ease of engagement, fair treatment, and the effectiveness of support available to vulnerable consumers. The findings will provide Ofgem with robust evidence on consumer preferences, including what consumers value most, the trade-offs they are willing to make, and the reasons underpinning those preferences. This will support informed decision-making on future policy and regulatory approaches to cost allocation and recovery, ensuring that consumer perspectives are appropriately reflected in Ofgem's considerations.

Notice.Title: DN815224 Lift Consultant - Project Manager
Notice.Description:
London Borough of Hackney is a Member of the Fusion 21 Members Consortium. This is a Direct Award for Cundalls from the established Fusion 21 Lifts Framework - Lot 5 Lift Consultancy.
The term of the contract will be for up to a 12 month period. It is anticipated that the contract will commence in September 2026.
The London Borough of Hackney is delivering a comprehensive Lift Modernisation Programme across its housing portfolio, comprising the replacement, refurbishment and upgrade of lift systems within occupied residential buildings. These works are critical to maintaining safe, reliable and accessible homes, particularly for residents who rely on lifts for day-to-day mobility.
The Council seeks to appoint a Lift Consultant to provide Project Management and Clerk of Works services to support the effective delivery of this Lift Modernisation programme, over a 12 month period. The Consultant's role is not limited to coordination, but extends to the provision of active oversight, independent assurance and quality control across all stages of delivery.
This commission is intended to ensure that works are delivered in a controlled and consistent manner, that risks are identified and managed proactively, and that the completed installations meet the Council's required standards in terms of safety, quality, compliance and resident experience. The Consultant shall act at all times in the interests of the Council, maintaining clear visibility of programme status, performance and emerging risks.
Notice.CpvDescription: Installation services of lifting and handling equipment, except lifts and escalators and Lifts and Mechanical lifts

Notice.Title: Transforming Access to Climate Finance in Somalia
Notice.Description:
The contract will provide technical assistance to ensure Somalia is progressively better positioned to mobilise, manage and coordinate increased flows of climate finance. It will focus on advising the Federal Government of Somalia on how best to operationalise an appropriate and well-structured National Climate Fund, with clear and inclusive governance arrangements, effective coordination mechanisms and transparent fiduciary systems. The focus will be on establishing practical institutional arrangements that can function reliably and build confidence among national counterparts and development partners.
The programme will advise on approaches to expand access to climate finance from multilateral funds, strengthen engagement with Somali private sector actors and wider civil society, and enhance national capacity across all relevant national stakeholders to prepare and advance a coherent and inclusive pipeline of climate relevant initiatives.

Royal Berkshire Fire Authority (RBFA) has an ongoing requirement for a licensing partner to support its technological and operational infrastructure. Notice.Title: PATH DELIVERY PHASE 2
Notice.Description:
HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) sought to appoint a Delivery Partner to support Phase 2 of the PATH (Pathways to Acceleration, Transformation and Human-centred delivery) programme within CDIO. PATH is HMRC's approach to accelerating the design, development and delivery of modern digital tax and customs services through improved ways of working, stronger governance, enhanced capability, and innovative delivery practices.
The requirement focused on embedding and maturing PATH as a sustainable operating model across HMRC by strengthening culture, delivery processes, governance arrangements, decision-making frameworks, communications, onboarding approaches, reporting structures and AI-enabled tooling. The successful supplier was required to work collaboratively with HMRC leadership and delivery teams to establish enduring capability, improve organisational effectiveness and support the transition of innovation activities into business as usual operations.
The services included management consultancy, organisational transformation, capability building, coaching and mentoring, delivery improvement, change management, governance development, knowledge transfer and continuous improvement activities. A key objective of the contract was to reduce dependency on external consultancy support by developing HMRC's internal capability and ensuring the effective transfer of knowledge, skills and responsibilities throughout the contract lifecycle.
The contract was awarded following a further competition under Crown Commercial Service Management Consultancy Framework Four (MCF4), Lot 3. Suppliers were evaluated on the basis of quality, social value and price, with award made to the Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT).
The initial contract term is 12 months commencing on 17 August 2026 and ending on 16 August 2027, with an option to extend for a further 12 months. The initial contract value is £2,500,000 excluding VAT, with a potential total contract value of up to £5,000,000 excluding VAT should the extension option be exercised.

Notice.Title: Data Warehouse Route to Cloud
Notice.Description:
Data Warehouse Route to Cloud service delivery. Support the design and delivery of a Cloud platform, the migration of data to this platform and the decommissioning of the legacy platform.
The service will be responsible for the design, development, and deployment of an alpha data platform, for supporting migration of data to this platform and the decommissioning of the legacy platform through beta and into live. This includes:
• Technical enablement and standing up of a new cloud-based platform • Migration of (c150Tb - to be validated) of data from legacy platform to the new cloud-based platform • Oversee the decommissioning of existing on-premises data infrastructure
All activities must align with DWP's governance standards, including compliance with the Digital Design Authority, Red Lines Assessment, and collaborative engagement with stakeholders across Digital and wider business units. The service is expected to work closely with DWP teams to ensure maximum business value and minimal disruption throughout the transformation.
The service will also provide ongoing support to DWP staff, ensuring knowledge transfer and operational readiness, and contributing to the department's strategic goal of a fully realised, cloud-native data warehousing estate.

Notice.Title: Tees SPA Intertidal Mudflats and Sandflats Biotope Mapping
Notice.Description:
The Teesmouth and Cleveland Coast Special Protection Area (SPA), located in north-east England, encompasses a diverse mosaic of coastal and estuarine habitats. Despite historic land loss due to industrial reclamation during the 19th and early 20th centuries, substantial areas of intertidal sand and mudflat, saltmarsh, freshwater grazing marsh, saline lagoon, sand dune, shingle, rocky shore, and shallow coastal waters remain. These habitats support a range of nationally and internationally important bird species. Originally classified in 1995 for its European importance in supporting breeding little tern, passage Sandwich tern, wintering red knot, and passage common redshank as well as an assemblage of over 20,000 waterbirds. The SPA was updated in 2000 and extended again in January 2020. The most recent extension added breeding avocet, breeding common tern, and non-breeding ruff as protected features, along with additional areas of coastal and wetland habitat, the River Tees channel, and the shallow waters of Tees Bay.
The estuary's intertidal mudflats are critical feeding grounds for SPA bird species, particularly waders. Seal Sands is the largest area of intertidal mudflat on the east coast of England between Lindisfarne and the Humber Estuary to the south (Figure 1). It supports high densities of invertebrate prey, especially for overwintering redshank and shelduck. However, ecological condition has declined in recent years due to the growth of opportunistic macroalgae [Opp Mac], which may be reducing food availability for key wader species. Smaller areas of intertidal mudflat occur elsewhere within the estuary, notably at Greatham Creek and Seal Sands (Figure 2), North Tees Mudflat (Figure 3). Sandy beaches such as North Gare Sands (Figure 4) and Bran Sands (Figure 5). These areas provide valuable foraging and roosting grounds for species such as red knot and sanderling and are integral to the SPA's ecological function and bird assemblage. To better understand the condition and ecological value of these habitats, we are seeking a contractor to carry out the following:
A Phase 1 and Phase 2 biotope survey, including sampling of sediment, including infauna and contaminants
Reporting

Notice.Title: GB-London: Consultancy Required for LondonEnergy Future Transport Yard Feasibility
Notice.Description:
LEL must establish whether the Hawley Road site can be retained or, if not, identify a suitable replacement capable of meeting current and future operational requirements before the lease expires in February 2030.
The key question is what constitutes the most deliverable, operationally suitable and value-for-money solution for providing LEL's transport yard facilities beyond February 2030.
LEL will therefore appoint a suitably qualified consultant to undertake a feasibility study and strategic options appraisal, assessing suitable alternatives and recommending a preferred option and next steps.
Based on LEL's estimated timescales for designing, constructing and transitioning into a new site, there is a need to undertake a feasibility study to identify alternative transport yard options as soon as possible, with a preferred way forward decided by June 2027. This timetable is intended to enable the preferred option to progress into design and procurement during 2027, followed by the necessary environmental assessment, planning and permitting activities and subject to approvals, construction. The Consultant shall therefore plan and deliver the commission to support timely decision-making and protect the overall programme ahead of the Hawley Road lease expiry in February 2030.
Notice.CpvDescription: Feasibility study and Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis and Pre-feasibility study and technological demonstration

Notice.Title: 999 Risk Assessment
Notice.Description: The Department for Science, Innovation & Technology (DSIT) is seeking to commission an independent Network and Cyber Risk Assessment of the UK Public Emergency Call Service (PECS), accessed via 999 and 112. PECS is the public's primary route to emergency help and is a critical national service relied on by the public, emergency services, Government and industry. Around 37 million 999/112 calls were made in 2025. This procurement is funded through the Integrated Security Fund (ISF) and is being led by DSIT's Telecoms Security and Resilience team within the Digital Infrastructure Directorate. DSIT leads UK Government policy on the resilience of the 999 service and provides the secretariat for the 999/112 Liaison Committee. The Committee brings together lead Government departments, Ofcom, emergency services, BT as the call handling agent, Communication Providers, devolved administrations and other relevant organisations. It provides a forum for technical and operational oversight of PECS, supports escalation of issues across the system, and maintains the PECS Code of Practice. On 25 June 2023, BT experienced a major technical failure affecting its role as the Centralised Handling Authority (CHA) for 999 calls in the UK. The fault lasted for over ten hours and resulted in almost 10,000 unique callers being unable to reach 999 or 112. This was the first significant disruption to the service in nearly 90 years. The outage prompted significant public concern and formal review activity, including Ofcom's review and Government's post-incident review. Those reviews highlighted weaknesses in cross-system visibility, response arrangements and the absence of a single set of comprehensive procedures or risk information across the end-to-end call chain. The 999/112 call chain is a multi-organisation system involving several interdependent parties: - Communication Providers (CPs) - who originate and route 999 calls from fixed-line, mobile, and VoIP networks; - BT as the Centralised Handling Authority (CHA) - which receives, triages and routes calls to the appropriate emergency authority; - Emergency Authorities (EAs) and their control rooms - including Police, Fire, Ambulance and Coastguard - which receive and handle the calls. In broad terms, a caller dials 999 or 112; the originating Communication Provider transfers the call to BT's CHA switch sites; BT's 999 call handling operation identifies the appropriate Emergency Authority and routes the call onward; and the receiving Emergency Authority control room determines and coordinates the emergency response. Risks can arise at any point in this chain, but are particularly likely to emerge at the interfaces between organisations, systems and contractual responsibilities. About The DWP:
The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) is the UK's largest public service department and is responsible for welfare, pensions, and child maintenance policy. The Department is responsible for administering the State Pension and a range of working age, disability, and ill health benefits to around 20 million claimants. The DWP operates on a scale that is almost unrivalled anywhere in Europe, and most people in Great Britain will encounter the DWP at some point in their lives.
The DWP delivers its services through a leasehold Estate, operating over 800 properties nationally. This includes job centres, assessment centres, corporate centres, and service centres. The DWP Estate is geographically dispersed and has a large footprint on UK high streets as it requires a local presence.

The new Security Guarding contract will focus on placing trained Security Officers (equipped with Body Worn Cameras and Private Mobile Radios) across the whole DWP estate, including Jobcentre Plus sites and Corporate Hubs. The contract also covers duties for reception services required at Caxton House, London and Quarry House, Leeds and a 24/7 keyholding service to respond to requests to unlock and lock DWP sites without automation available through Critical Security Infrastructure Programme upgrades.
The appointed Security Guarding Supplier will work closely with Authority, the Total Facilities Management Supplier, Security Control Centre Supplier and other members of the Authority's Estates department supply chain to ensure the safety and security of the Authority's employees, customers, and property.

Notice.Title: Managed Service for Blood Grouping Assays and Consumables
Notice.Description: Provision of automated blood transfusion analysers, associated reagents, consumables, maintenance and support services for Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. This contract is being awarded via the NHSSC PCR 2015 Laboratory Diagnostics, Point of Care Testing & Pathology Managed Services OJEU REF - 2023/S 000-028831 Framework Agreement using the Direct Award mechanism. The contract covers the supply, installation, validation, calibration, maintenance and ongoing support of automated transfusion analysers used by Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust to perform blood grouping, antibody screening, further investigations and serological cross-matching. These functions are critical to the safe provision of blood and blood components for transfusion and support compliance with relevant regulatory and clinical standards. The service includes the provision of analysers, reagents, consumables, quality control materials, software support and upgrades, preventative maintenance, technical support, fault resolution and user training. The supplier will also provide ongoing contract support, manage reagent supply in line with clinical activity, investigate analytical errors and equipment issues, and deliver agreed service levels and performance standards. Automated testing and the electronic transfer of validated results are mandatory requirements for the Electronic Issue (EI) of blood. EI enables the rapid issue of compatible blood products, reducing blood wastage, improving stock management and supporting the timely treatment of patients across emergency departments, operating theatres, maternity services, critical care units, haematology services and other clinical areas. The contract supports a Trust-wide critical clinical service for patients requiring transfusion, patients at risk of major blood loss, and antenatal patients and their babies. Continuity of analyser availability, reagent supply and technical support is essential to maintaining patient safety, regulatory compliance and operational resilience. Any interruption to the service could adversely affect the Trust's ability to provide timely and safe transfusion support, potentially impacting emergency care, surgical procedures, maternity pathways and other critical patient services. The contract is therefore essential to ensuring the uninterrupted delivery of a safe, reliable and compliant transfusion service across Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust Estimated Annual Test Performed • Blood Group 50,000 • Antibody Screen 50,000 • Antibody Panel 1,500 • Antibody Titre 15 • Crossmatch 1500 • RhK Phenotype 1000 • Other Phenotypes 180 • Direct Antiglobulin Test 650

Notice.Title: Bangladesh Carbon Market Governance & Readiness Sprint
Notice.Description:
The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the government of Bangladesh.
Bangladesh is establishing the foundations for participation in high-integrity carbon markets, including Article 6, CORSIA and voluntary carbon markets. While progress has been made through the establishment of a carbon market framework and supporting governance arrangements, further support is needed to operationalise these systems across government, strengthen institutional coordination, and enable Bangladesh to use carbon markets to support delivery of its NDC 3.0 unconditional mitigation targets.
The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance and capacity building to strengthen Bangladesh's carbon market governance, authorisation processes, MRV, reporting and institutional readiness. Working with relevant government agencies, including MoEFCC, DoE, the Power Division, Ministry of Finance and other line ministries, the project will support practical implementation of carbon market rules, CORSIA readiness, UNFCCC reporting requirements, and inclusive, high-integrity market participation.
Key outputs are expected to include governance and coordination tools, an authorisation and safeguards toolkit, CORSIA readiness and reporting support, a structured government capacity-building programme, and sector readiness briefs identifying future carbon market investment opportunities. The project aims to strengthen Bangladesh's ability to participate in high-integrity carbon markets, unlock climate finance, improve institutional capability, and support implementation of national climate targets.
Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk

Amey have been tasked by the DIO through the FDIS to deliver the Regional Accommodation Maintenance Service for the Central and North Regions.
This notice is a call for competition and there may not be a further notice related to this opportunity.
For Amey to accept any EoI it is ESSENTIAL that any subcontractor is: • willing to act as Main Contractor (essential requirement); • a Verified member of Constructionline (GOLD), relevant Work Category MUST show that Subcontracting is possible, and the 'Building Safety Act - Standard Construction' must be Verified; • capable of working to MOD SFG20 (PPM works only); • capable of working in a BIM Level 2 environment (where applicable); • compliant with DefStan 05-138 (required if you are likely to handle MoD Identifiable Information on your IT system); • willing to work with Amey to deliver Social Value to our Client; ideally, complete the Social Value Goal within the Constructionline platform.
DESIRABLE attributes of our Supply Chain: • have a Corporate Social Responsibility policy; • have a Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan
If successful the subcontractor will need to pass a PQQ, sign up to Amey Terms and Conditions, and meet the MoD Security Requirements.
This future opportunity notice is for Expressions of Interest, BY EMAIL ONLY.
Procurement Documentation will follow separately via a link from our e-tender portal (Curtis Fitch).
Note 1: The bidder must quote for all aspects of the Works. Note 2: Future works of a similar nature may be negotiated based upon submitted rates. Note 3: Those making an Expression of Interest will be required to sign-up to our 'Sub-contract Agreement' where 'Mini Competitions' or 'Call Offs' will be used to tender works/services. Note 4: For complex projects such as External Wall Insulation installation, Structural works etc. it is a requirement that the bidder must (at Contract Award) carry PI Insurance cover of not less than £1,000,000. Note 5: Those making an EoI will be assessed in accordance with the Public Contract Regulations 2015 i.e. Regulations 57, 58 & 60. ADS expressly reserves the right to require those making an EoI to provide additional information supplementing or clarifying any of the information requested. Note 6: Depending on Amey's annual spend with individual bidders you may be required to either have committed to the Science Based Targets Initiative (SBTi), set SBTi approved near-term targets, or Net Zero targets.
This opportunity is not advertised on Constructionline.
ADS does not bind itself to accept any tender and is not liable for any costs incurred by those expressing an interest or tendering for this opportunity.

Notice.Title: Face to Face Translation Services Contract
Notice.Description:
This procurement is being undertaken jointly by:
University Hospitals Plymouth NHS Trust
Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
Torbay and South Devon NHS Foundation Trust
Devon Partnership NHS Trust
Livewell Southwest CIC
Collectively referred to throughout this specification as the Participating Organisations.
The Participating Organisations require the provision of a professionally managed Face to Face Foreign Language Interpretation Service to support communication between patients, carers and healthcare professionals where English is not the patient's first or preferred language.
The purpose of this procurement is to establish replacement arrangements for existing contracts and to secure a high quality, efficient and reliable interpretation service that supports patient safety, equitable access to healthcare services and a positive patient experience. Notice.Title: Independent Evaluation of the Better Security, Better Care Programme (October 2025 to October 2028)
Notice.Description:
Digital Care Hub is seeking an independent evaluation partner to assess the delivery, impact, sustainability and value for money of the Better Security, Better Care (BSBC) programme. Funded by the Department of Health and Social Care, BSBC supports approximately 28,000 CQC-registered adult social care locations in England to improve cyber security, data protection and information governance, including compliance with the Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT). Delivery is led nationally by Digital Care Hub through more than 30 Local Support Organisations, combining central leadership, guidance, training, communications, data analysis and performance management with trusted local support.
The supplier will design and deliver a proportionate mixed-method evaluation covering programme governance and delivery, stakeholder engagement, partner effectiveness, reach, changes in awareness and behaviour, adoption of good practice, DSPT outcomes, organisational resilience, wider benefits, cost effectiveness, return on investment and social and economic value. The work should identify lessons, good practice and evidence-based recommendations while providing ongoing insight to support continuous improvement.
Key deliverables are an evaluation framework and inception report within three months; ongoing data collection, analysis and stakeholder engagement; monthly progress meetings; an interim report by September 2027; and a final evaluation report, shorter executive report, presentation and dissemination-ready outputs by October 2028. Close-down and dissemination support will continue to March 2029.
The proposed contract runs from October 2026 to March 2029, with a maximum budget of £125,000 inclusive of VAT. Bidders must demonstrate strong experience in programme and economic evaluation, publicly funded programmes, mixed-method research, stakeholder engagement and report writing. Knowledge of adult social care, health and care systems, cyber security, digital transformation or information governance is required.
Tender responses must include organisation and personnel details, methodology, data collection and analysis plans, delivery timetable, resourcing, quality assurance, risk management, up to three relevant examples, a full pricing schedule, assumptions and proposed social value. Evaluation weightings are: understanding 15%, methodology 35%, experience 20%, project management 10%, social value 10% and price 10%. The supplier must comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, confidentiality, insurance, procurement, equality and safeguarding requirements. Clarification questions are due by 14 October 2026 and tenders by 18 October 2026. Please see attachment for full specifications.

Notice.Title: GB-Maidstone: Preliminary Market Engagement via GCA Framework - Brief Project Portfolio Management Solution
Notice.Description:
Kent Fire and Rescue Service (KFRS) is exploring options for a Project Portfolio Management (PPM) solution to support the planning, management, oversight and reporting of projects and programmes across the organisation. KFRS is open to different solution and delivery models, including established Software as a Service (SaaS) products and Microsoft/Power Platform-based solutions. Please note: For the purposes of this market engagement, KFRS is only seeking responses in respect of solutions which are currently available for procurement through an existing Government Commercial Agency (GCA) framework (formerly CCS). Suppliers should identify the relevant framework, Lot (where applicable) and service/solution listing within their response. The purpose of this exercise is to undertake a short and proportionate test of the market before KFRS determines its procurement strategy and route to market. In particular, KFRS wishes to understand: •what potentially suitable solutions are available within or around the stated affordability envelope; •the broad alignment of available products with KFRS's functional and technical requirements; •the different solution and service models available and the respective responsibilities of KFRS and the supplier; •indicative licensing/subscription, implementation, support and ongoing configuration/development costs; •the extent to which solutions allow KFRS to retain appropriate control and portability of its organisational data; •any observations from the market which may help KFRS refine its requirements; and •the specific GCA/CCS framework, Lot and/or service listing through which the proposed solution can be procured.
Nature of this Exercise This is a preliminary market engagement exercise and not a competitive procurement or invitation to tender. The functional and technical requirements provided with this brief represent KFRS's current understanding of its needs. They are being provided to give suppliers sufficient information to determine whether they have a product or solution that could potentially meet the requirement. Suppliers are not required to provide a detailed response against each individual requirement or complete the requirements schedules on a line-by-line basis. Responses will not be evaluated or scored as tender submissions. Instead, KFRS is seeking a brief, high-level response that will enable us to understand whether a proposed solution appears sufficiently aligned with our needs to warrant further exploration. KFRS would also welcome constructive feedback on the requirements themselves. This may include identifying areas which would benefit from clarification, or alternative approaches or current market capabilities which KFRS should consider. Please respond via the Kent Business Portal.

Notice.Title: Passenger Lift Replacement Within Diplomatic Mission
Notice.Description: This project involves the refurbishment and upgrade of the existing passenger lift installation at CH, London. The scope includes the full removal and replacement of the lift car, associated shaft equipment, and integration with the building's lift controls and life safety systems. Works are to be undertaken in a live, high-security diplomatic building, requiring strict adherence to security protocols, with minimal disruption to operations. The contract requires the provision of a compliant lift installation in accordance with BS EN 81-72:2020, BS 9999, and relevant Building Regulations, including Approved Document B. All works must meet or exceed the performance, safety, and accessibility standards expected for lift installations in a commercial/public building setting. Contractors will be expected to coordinate closely with heritage, building services, and security stakeholders, ensuring integration with existing infrastructure and minimal aesthetic impact on listed features. Specific interface requirements include BMS integration, fire alarm interlocks, and mechanical ventilation enhancements within the shaft to meet smoke control provisions. The successful contractor will be required to deliver a complete design, supply, installation, testing, and commissioning package, inclusive of all enabling works, builders' work in connection, and certification. NOTE: To register your interest in this notice and obtain any additional information please visit the myTenders Web Site at https://www.mytenders.co.uk/Search/Search_Switch.aspx?ID=234380. The buyer has indicated that it will accept electronic responses to this notice via the Postbox facility. A user guide is available at https://www.mytenders.co.uk/sitehelp/help_guides.aspx. Notice.Title: Age-friendly Training
Notice.Description:
The Centre for Ageing Better is seeking a contractor to lead the research, design, and development of age-friendly training products that will support customer facing organisations be more age-friendly.
The Age-friendly Training project aims to improve the quality and uptake of age-friendly training across the UK, helping more staff in customer-facing settings to have the understanding and motivation to make services more accessible and inclusive for older people.
The successful bidder will lead a design process - understanding needs and co-producing training with those who may be implementing or receiving the final training. They will research the current age-friendly training landscape, identify what training products are needed for different audiences, and develop, test and refine training products that can be used by age-friendly communities and other organisations across diverse local contexts.
The successful bidder will bring expertise in producing training products related to topics such as EDI, accessibility, health inequalities and service delivery. They will have a good understanding of the types of training approaches that are effective to enable learning and behaviour change of those working in customer-facing settings.

Notice.Title: Procurement Purchase to Pay System
Notice.Description:
Maximus is undertaking a procurement exercise to identify a strategic Source-to-Pay (S2P) platform to support the ongoing transformation of procurement processes across the organisation. The solution will be expected to support an integrated procurement lifecycle, including:
• Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) • Strategic Sourcing • Supplier Management • Procure-to-Pay (P2P) • Invoice Automation • Spend Analytics & Reporting
SAP will remain the organisation's finance platform and system of record. The primary objectives of this procurement are to improve procurement governance, contract visibility, supplier management, user experience, process compliance and reporting capabilities while maintaining seamless integration with SAP. Key Evaluation Priorities The evaluation will place particular emphasis on:
1. SAP Integration Capability (Critical) 2. Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) 3. User Experience and Adoption 4. End-to-End Source-to-Pay Functionality 5. Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)
Mandatory Requirements: Suppliers will be required to confirm compliance with all of the following mandatory requirements. Failure to meet any of these criteria may result in exclusion from the next stage of the procurement process. SAP Integration (Critical) • Proven, standard integration capability with SAP ECC and/or SAP S/4HANA, SAP by Design. • Ability to integrate core procurement and financial data. • Demonstrable customer references utilising SAP-integrated deployments. Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) • Provision of a mature Contract Lifecycle Management capability. • Support for contract repository, metadata management, approval workflows, version control and contract renewal management. • Ability to link contracts with suppliers, sourcing events and procurement activity. 3. Global Operating Model • Ability to support multiple countries, currencies, languages and tax jurisdictions. • Experience supporting global or multi-region organisations. 4. Security & Compliance • ISO 27001 certification / Cyber Essentials Plus • GDPR compliance. • Role-based access controls. • Audit logging and traceability of user activity. • Appropriate business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements. 5. Enterprise-Scale Experience • Demonstrated experience delivering S2P and/or P2P solutions for large enterprise organisations. • Ability to provide relevant customer references for organisations of comparable size and complexity. 6. Delivery & Support Capability • Availability of UK-based implementation and support resources. • Ability to provide ongoing support for global business operations. • Proven implementation methodology and support model. Supplier Response Suppliers are requested to confirm whether they meet each of the mandatory requirements outlined above and provide a brief summary of their relevant experience and capabilities.

Notice.Title: Major Water Infrastructure Programme (MWIP) - Programmatic Delivery and Opportunity Assessment
Notice.Description:
Direct Award from Government Commercial Agency, Management Consultancy Four Framework (MCF4) (RM6309) Lot 8: Infrastructure.
Undertake a programme-wide Value for Money (VfM) appraisal of the Major Water Infrastructure Programme (MWIP) to identify, test and prioritise credible cost reduction and VfM opportunities, with a focus on decisions that can influence cost, schedule, risk and deliverability at the early stages of the project lifecycle across identified VfM drivers.
The study will adopt a two-stage approach to delivery. Stage 1 will provide a programme-wide VfM assessment, covering VfM drivers and identifying, testing and prioritising credible opportunities. Greater emphasis will be placed on those drivers where there is currently greatest potential to influence VfM, particularly given the maturity of assets within the Reservoir Programme.
Stage 2 will comprise subsequent steps required to further develop, evidence and unlock priority opportunities identified through Stage 1. These may include targeted technical, commercial or delivery assessments, where required. Any such subsequent work will be defined and commissioned separately based on the findings and recommendations from Stage 1.
The objectives of the Services are to:
• Identify potential VfM drivers across MWIP.
• Challenge and develop the initial opportunities through structured input from relevant industry and technical experts.
• Identify and prioritise the most significant opportunities for further assessment.
• Quantify potential benefits, where sufficient evidence is available, including potential cost and schedule benefits and wider value.
• Assess each priority opportunity against cost, schedule, risk, deliverability, commercial implications and wider value.
• Identify key assumptions, evidence gaps, confidence levels, dependencies, enabling conditions and risks.
• Assess the implications for delivery approaches, governance, commercial models and wider system enablers.
• Identify opportunities that may be applicable across the wider Reservoir Programme and, where relevant, other asset types in MWIP.
• Develop practical recommendations for taking priority opportunities forward.
• Provide Ofwat and relevant stakeholders with a robust and transparent evidence base to support decision-making.
Scope of Services
The Supplier shall be responsible for determining the appropriate methodology, approach and activities required to achieve the purpose and objectives of the Services.
Outputs / Deliverables
The Supplier shall provide a VfM Appraisal Report and Prioritised VfM Opportunity Matrix setting out, where evidence permits.

Notice.Title: GB-Cromer: PROC158 Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) Services to support preparation of Local Plan
Notice.Description: The Council is seeking to appoint suitably qualified consultants to provide SEA services throughout the preparation of the Local Plan. The commission will include the preparation of the SEA Scoping Report, Environmental Reports and associated SEA documentation at key stages of plan preparation, together with ongoing advice and support to ensure the SEA process is effectively integrated with the Council's Local Plan programme. SEA is an iterative process that runs alongside Local Plan preparation, helping to identify, describe and evaluate the likely significant effects of the emerging Local Plan and reasonable alternatives. Government guidance on the new plan making system confirms the expectation that new local plans will need to undertake Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) if certain criteria set out under Regulation 5 of The Environmental Assessment of Plans and Programmes Regulations 2004 are met. Furthermore, the Government has stated that they consider that all local plans will need to carry out SEA. Therefore, the Council requires SEA to inform the preparation of the new Local Plan.

NHS Supply Chain: Food sought to establish a non-exclusive DPS Agreement for the supply of Food To Go to NHS Supply Chain: Food's customer base via the Direct Route covering products including but not limited to: Patient Feeding Sandwiches, Salads, and Snack pots. Notice.Title: Pakistan NDC 3.0 Delivery Coordination Mechanism (Federal-Provincial Coordination and Tracking)
Notice.Description:
The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the Government of Pakistan.
Pakistan has committed to reducing projected greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2035 through its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0. Delivering this target will depend heavily on action at the provincial level, where responsibility for many climate-relevant sectors rests. While the Government of Pakistan has established new coordination arrangements through the National Climate Finance Strategy (NCFS), challenges remain around federal-provincial coordination, implementation tracking, climate finance visibility, and reporting progress against national climate commitments.
The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance to support the Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination (MoCC&EC), the Pakistan Climate Change Authority (PCCA), and provincial governments to establish and operationalise a practical federal-provincial coordination and tracking mechanism for NDC 3.0 implementation. The project will strengthen institutional coordination, improve monitoring and reporting of climate actions and investments, build government capacity, and support the mobilisation of climate finance. The intervention will also integrate Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) considerations to promote more inclusive climate governance and decision-making.
Key outputs are expected to include a federal-provincial NDC coordination framework, a standardised NDC tracking and reporting framework, an interoperability pilot connecting existing government climate and public-sector data systems, operational support for a Tactical Climate Coordination Forum, and a sustainability and scale-up roadmap. The project aims to strengthen Pakistan's ability to implement and report on its climate commitments, improve evidence-based decision-making, enhance transparency and accountability, and create a stronger foundation for attracting climate finance and accelerating NDC delivery across provinces and sectors.
Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk.

Notice.Title: GB-London: 1008157290 T1414 Testing the feasibility of the use of solar reflective solutions on rolling stock
Notice.Description:
T1414 aims to demonstrate the effective use of Solar Reflective Solutions to reduce internal vehicle temperatures, supporting improved passenger comfort, reduced HVAC energy consumption demand and improved component reliability for GB passenger rolling stock.
Work Package 1- Benchmarking and trial planning • Assess the current performance of existing rolling stock paint systems to establish a baseline against which the potential benefit and disbenefits of adopting solar reflective alternatives can be determined. • Identify and select SRSs which meet GB passenger rolling stock requirements to ensure the SRSs trialled meet technical, safety, and operational material requirements. • Develop a test plan for a box trial, representative of a rail vehicle, to assess the effect that SRSs would have on internal rail vehicle temperature. Work Package 2 - Box trials • Undertake box trials2, representative of a rail vehicle, as per the test plan produced in WP1, to gather data on the solar, thermal and operational environment performance of SRSs. •Analyse the data gathered from the box trials to enable cost-benefit analysis of the material systems and mitigate potential risk/unsuitable candidates. Work Package 3 - Business case for SRS adoption • Produce an initial business case for the use of SRSs on GB passenger rolling stock based on WP2. Work Package 4 - Planning next steps - This will only be undertaken if business case in WP3 is positive • Identify the questions (including technical) that remain to be answered to make informed decisions on the adoption of SRS. • Develop a test plan for trial(s) that would answer the outstanding questions identified in WP 2 and 3 so RSSB may seek support from relevant parties and plan for such trial(s). Note - The decision to proceed with the last work package will be made by RSSB based on the findings from WP2 and 3. The work for WP4 should be included in the total price, but with the cost separately identified to be able to be removed if WP4 is not progressed.

Notice.Title: Cheshire and Warrington Outline Water Plan
Notice.Description:
The newly established Cheshire and Warrington Combined Authority (CWCA) has recently stated its intention to commission an Independent Economic Review (IER) for the subregion - setting out the evidence for the opportunities for and constraints on local growth. In support of this, it is vital to better understand where water infrastructure may require upgrades to support local ambition, and how we can better work together to ensure that flooding and drought are not impediments to growth whilst ensuring that wider ecosystem services and farming resilience are better supported.
Simultaneously, the Water White Paper published in January 2026 committed Government to act on the Independent Water Commission recommendation, setting up Regional Systems Planning in England. DEFRA have set out an intention to pilot this through Regional System Planners (RSPs), established across each region of England with the aim of influencing both PR29 and other water system investment plans. Defra are keen for partnerships to pilot RSP governance and structures during this set-up year. and have set out that they only intend to provide high level direction on form. Within this context there is a significant opportunity to influence water planning, and ensure alignment with local growth and wider environmental ambitions.
To support the IER along with engagement with the establishing North West RSP, ECW is seeking to appoint consultants to develop a strategic, place based evidence base and outline water plan that sits between national/regional water planning processes and local spatial, economic, and infrastructure planning.

Notice.Title: CA18475 - RFQ2026/35 - NMANDD PEACEPLUS Mourne Film Festival Project - Rural Women's Voices.
Notice.Description:
Competent Consultancy companies are hereby invited to tender to design, develop and deliver NMANDD PEACEPLUS Mourne International Film Festival Project; Rural Women's Voices. The aim is to deliver and design a community-led creative programme empowering women from the Mourne DEA (District Electoral Area) to develop their voices through creative writing and filmmaking culminating in a 20-minute original film created by participants that will be premiered at an International Film Festival celebrating Rural Women in the week of International Women's Day 8th March 2027. The women will plan the film festival selecting films that reflect the lives of rural women around the world. This project aims to amplify underrepresented rural women's stories, connecting local experiences with global perspectives.
To access this competition:
Registered: Login to https://suppliers.multiquote.com and view the opportunity CA18475.
Not registered: Visit https://suppliers.multiquote.com then register and quote CA18475 as the reason for registration.
Any queries please contact MultiQuote on 020 3920 8054.

Notice.Description:
The Big Peat Conversation - A Public Dialogue on Land Use in England's Lowland Agricultural Peatlands.
This research project aims to engage a diverse and inclusive group of members of the public through a series of deliberative workshops to explore the role of lowland peatlands in achieving goals around the environment, farming and economic growth. > To learn and understand public and community views and perspectives towards the future role of lowland peatlands and what underlies them. > To Identify key principles and priorities to help resolve competing land use demands in lowland peatlands. It is also possible that these findings could be taken into consideration when designing future policy.

Notice.Title: Creative Sector Services CIC (t/a Creative United) Take it away Scheme Credit Provider Contract
Notice.Description:
A tender opportunity is offered by Creative Sector Services CIC (trading as Creative United), for the provision of consumer credit services for the Take it away Scheme (the Scheme) commencing 1 November 2026 for a period of 18 months, with provision for Creative United to extend the contract for two (2) further twelve (12) month periods (subject to performance review in accordance with the terms and conditions of contract) up to a maximum of forty-two(42) months in total.
The Take it away Scheme is a publicly funded initiative designed to make it more affordable for people to get involved in learning and playing music by providing interest free loans of between £100 and £25,000 for the purchase of musical instruments, equipment, software any other associated goods or services they may need (such as a block of tuition) in order to get started or further develop their music practice.
Creative United's objective is to use the Take it away scheme to support creative livelihoods by providing affordable access to musical instruments to people of all ages and abilities across the UK, working in partnership with musical instrument retailers and other organisations across the music sector.
The Scheme is open to all qualifying UK residents over the age of 18 (subject to status) and made available via a network of approved musical instrument retailers in England. A variation of the scheme in partnership with the Arts Council of Northern Ireland is available exclusively to Northern Ireland Residents over the age of 18.
The awarded contract would cover the provision of the Scheme through the network of retailers in England and in Northern Ireland. The opportunity may also exist during the term of the awarded contract for the Scheme to be extended to include a network of retailers in Wales and/or Scotland subject to the agreement and financial support of their respective Arts Councils (or other funders) in due course. For the avoidance of doubt the inclusion of Scotland and Wales is not guaranteed but is included as a potential enlargement of the Scheme for the purposes of this procurement, subject to the caveat above.
Under our current funding agreement with ACE, our priority is to support customers that fall into one or more of the following target categories: - Customers earning below the median UK wage of £34,000 - Customers living in areas of low participation in the arts (as reported by the Department for Culture Media and Sport, and the Office of National Statistics - Customers purchasing a musical instrument for the first time - Customers that identify as disabled (or purchasing on behalf of a disabled person)
To apply: You should complete and return a copy of our attached Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) by 17 July 2026.
All supporting documents including the Invitation to Tender (ITT) which includes the specifics of the contract are available to download from this notice.

Notice.Title: Contributing to Ending the Preventable Deaths of mothers, babies and children by 2030 (EPD)
Notice.Description:
Contributing to Ending the Preventable Deaths of mothers, babies and children by 2030 (EPD) is a UK government commitment and is a core health objective within the International Development Strategy. It is also central to FCDO's priority on women and girls and humanitarian efforts. The approach focuses on addressing the issues affecting the health and rights of women, babies and children.
The burden of deaths remains huge - newborn deaths make up the greatest number of deaths from any cause in low-income countries. Women and girls' rights are at threat and increasingly politicised. The solutions are harder than ever, requiring high quality, accessible and affordable health systems, women empowered to access care and an organised approach to development diplomacy and policy influencing. Most deaths now occur in fragile and conflict affected settings and amongst the most marginalised people.
The FCDO's Human Development Department leads on the delivery of EPD. The EPD campaign focuses on 11 flagship countries and aims to contribute to reducing mortality rates in these by between 5-10% by 2030.
This EPD Support Programme will provide technical assistance (TA) to target country and central FCDO teams to complement UK investments that contribute to EPD across three of the four pillars within the approach paper. These are 1) strong health systems; 2) human rights, gender and equality, including sexual and reproductive health and rights; and 3) healthier environments including WASH, climate and health, nutrition and air pollution.
This will be one of the essential programmes in a new EPD Centre of Expertise to provide a timely and flexible offer of support across a range of areas, adopting a cross-cutting approach and using a range of modalities. This programme focuses on specific policy, alignment or evidence gaps. It will provide a varied TA offer from quick, specific responses to longer term technical inputs and EPD partnerships. The website has three key areas, The Supplier Directory, The Opportunities Map and The Supply Chain Promise through which it aims to make opportunities, visible, accessible and winnable. The platform is currently undergoing some significant changes and we need to ensure that the medium term development of the site, along with hosting and maintenance of the platform is contracted to ensure it is robust and current. We would like to partner with an experienced, agile and ambitious organisation to support the ongoing hosting, maintenance and development of the website. We are looking to secure a 2.5 year contract (September 2026 - March 2029) to ensure operational continuity and commercial viability.
